items.question: When must pitot heating be selected to AUTO or ON?
items.explanation: Pitot heating must be AUTO or ON at indicated OAT of +4 °C or less.

items.question: When must pitot heating be selected to AUTO or OFF?
items.explanation: Pitot heating must be AUTO or OFF at indicated OAT of +5 °C or more.

items.question: Is flight into known icing conditions permitted?
options: Yes, if pitot heating is ON
No, unless cold weather kit installed
items.explanation: Flight into known icing conditions is prohibited.

items.question: Is flight into freezing rain or freezing fog permitted?
options: Yes, if pitot heat is ON
items.explanation: Flight into freezing rain and freezing fog is prohibited.

items.question: What is the maximum crosswind component for Category A operation?
items.explanation: Maximum cross wind component must not exceed 20 kt (10 m/s).

items.question: Is take-off with a tailwind component permitted?
items.explanation: Take-Off with tail wind component is prohibited.

items.question: Are aerobatic manoeuvres permitted?
items.explanation: Aerobatic manoeuvres are prohibited.

items.question: Are practice autorotative landings permitted?
items.explanation: Practice autorotative landings are prohibited.

items.question: During autorotation, may ENG MODE switches be selected from FLIGHT to IDLE?
options: Yes, if both engines are operating
items.explanation: During autorotation the ENG MODE switches must NOT be selected from FLIGHT to IDLE except in an emergency.

items.question: What is the maximum slope for nose-up take-off or landing?
items.explanation: Sloped take-off/landing nose up is limited to 10°.

items.question: What is the maximum slope for nose-down take-off or landing?
items.explanation: Sloped take-off/landing nose down is limited to 7°.

items.question: What is the maximum slope for left or right wing low take-off or landing?
items.explanation: Left wing low and right wing low are each limited to 10°.

items.question: What is the maximum baggage compartment load?
items.explanation: Maximum baggage compartment load is 250 kg (550 lb).

items.question: What is the maximum unit load in the baggage compartment?
items.explanation: Maximum unit load is 450 kg/m² (92 lb/sq.ft).

items.question: What is the maximum cargo height in the baggage compartment?
items.explanation: Cargo height must not exceed 600 mm (2 ft).

items.question: During AEO flight, torque is above 100% and the aircraft is accelerating through 105 KIAS. Which limitation is relevant?
options: This is allowed as long as the aircraft remains below VNE
AEO flight with TQ above 100% is limited to 90 KIAS
This is allowed for 10 seconds as a transient torque condition
The limitation only applies during OEI operation
items.explanation: The RFM states that maximum airspeed in AEO with TQ above 100% is 90 KIAS.

items.question: You are flying an IFR approach at 7000 ft. What is the maximum IFR approach airspeed according to the AW169 limitation?
items.explanation: Maximum IFR approach speed is 130 KIAS up to 5000 ft, then reduced by 2 kt per 1000 ft above 5000 ft. At 7000 ft: 130 - 4 = 126 KIAS.

items.question: In OEI flight, TQ is indicating 150%. How should this be interpreted?
options: It is within the OEI maximum continuous range
It is within the OEI 2.5 minute range
It is only permitted as a 10-second transient
It exceeds the maximum OEI 2.5 minute limitation
items.explanation: For OEI transmission torque, maximum continuous is 140%, the 2.5 minute range is 141-174%, and the 10-second transient limit is 192%.

items.question: A running landing is planned on a prepared grass surface. What is the maximum ground speed for the running landing?
items.explanation: On prepared grass surfaces, maximum taxi speed is 20 knots GS, maximum rolling take-off or running landing speed is 30 knots GS, and maximum emergency landing speed is 50 knots GS.
references: AW169 RFM Section 1 - Ground Speed Limitations (p.1-11)

items.question: During engine start, ITT briefly reaches 810 °C for approximately one second. Which statement is correct?
options: This exceeds the engine start limitation because 750 °C is an absolute maximum
This is within the transient start allowance, provided the transient does not exceed 2 seconds
This is within the AEO 30-minute take-off range
This is only permitted during OEI operation
items.explanation: For engine starting, maximum ITT is 750 °C, with a transient allowance up to 825 °C for 2 seconds.
